name: Michal
charge: Despising the king in her heart for dancing before the ark
summary: As the ark came into the city of David with shouting and trumpets, Michal, Saul's daughter, watched from a window and despised David in her heart for leaping and dancing. She met him with contempt: how glorious was the king of Israel to day.
offense: Michal had once warned David of Saul's attempt upon his life and helped him escape through a window (1 Samuel 19:11-17). But when she saw him leaping and dancing before the Lord as the ark entered the city, she despised him in her heart (2 Samuel 6:16). An earlier act of loyalty did not prevent contempt from taking root later. David had laid aside the display of royal greatness for the service of that day. Chronicles describes him clothed in a robe of fine linen and wearing an ephod of linen (1 Chronicles 15:27). Michal's rebuke treated his public rejoicing as a disgrace before the handmaids. Her concern was how the king appeared in the eyes of servants, while David answered concerning the Lord before whom he rejoiced. David did not attribute the throne to his own dignity. He said that the Lord had chosen him before her father and his house, appointing him ruler over Israel (2 Samuel 6:21). The office was a gift, not a reason to consider himself too great to rejoice before its giver. The king's answer exposed the difference between honouring the Lord and guarding an image of personal importance.
judgment: David declared that he would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and that the maidservants Michal had mentioned would honour him (2 Samuel 6:22). Her scorn did not govern his worship. He would not make royal appearance the measure of what was fitting before God. The account closes with Michal having no child unto the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:23). Her place as Saul's daughter and David's wife did not turn the contempt into a small matter. The final word upon the encounter was not the preservation of her dignity, but the absence of children. The ark's arrival had brought sacrifices, gifts of food to the people, and David's return to bless his household. Michal met that return with reproach. The contrast is within the house itself: David came to bless, while she condemned the humility with which he had honoured the Lord.

entries.commentary: David gathered together thirty thousand chosen men of Israel. Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines, but everyone in the body is important in some way; the members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed. David and all the people went from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims. The ark had been taken from Israel by the Philistines in the days of the judges because of sin, and it had been left in the house of Abinadab. Through the wilderness there had been no house for the Lord, so the ark was moved from place to place. They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

When they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, the oxen shook the cart, and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark. The anger of the Lord was kindled, and God smote him for his error, and he died there by the ark. Only chosen men could come near the ark. The Lord had warned Aaron not to come at all times into the holy place before the mercy seat that he die not, and had set many stipulations upon it, even after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire. The Most High is holy and not to be handled carelessly. Grabbing the ark was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared it holy and untouchable. Everything in that day had to be done to a T; we owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ, for the Lord was not playing about His commandments. David was displeased that the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah, and he was afraid of the Lord that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? David had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of Him and His judgments. David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

When David heard the Lord had blessed the house of Obededom because of the ark, he went and brought up the ark to the city of David with gladness. When those that bore it had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings. David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod. He was happy and in the spirit, for the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people. Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet. Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High. David set the ark in the tabernacle he had pitched for it, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts. He dealt to every one, both men and women, a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine, and the people departed to their houses.

David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself. She had watched from a distance and could think only of the king dancing with his clothes falling, when the Most High had just brought the ark of God back among Israel. She forgot the greatness of the day and let a murmuring spirit take her. David answered that he danced before the Lord who chose him before her father to be ruler over Israel, therefore he would play before the Lord, and would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants he would be had in honor. Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.

David prepared a place and pitched a tent for the ark in the city of David. He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever. -

David assembled all Israel and the chief Levites by their families, naming the sons of Kohath, Merari, Gershom, Elizaphan, Hebron, and Uzziel with their chiefs and numbers. He called for the priests Zadok and Abiathar and for the Levites, showing the Most High had set a clear structure among the priesthood.

David charged the chief fathers of the Levites to sanctify themselves before bringing up the ark, because the first attempt failed when they did not seek him after the due order. The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High. -

David appointed Levites as singers with psalteries, harps, and cymbals, to lift up the voice with joy. Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed to sound cymbals of brass; others played harps and psalteries; the priests blew the trumpets before the ark, and doorkeepers were set. Every rank had its assigned place.

David and the elders and captains went to bring up the ark from the house of Obededom with joy. When the Most High helped the Levites bearing the ark, they offered seven bullocks and seven rams. David was clothed in a robe of fine linen along with the Levites and singers, and wore an ephod of linen. The people were dressed well, and the same custom carried down through Solomon.

All Israel brought up the ark with shouting, cornet, trumpets, cymbals, psalteries, and harps. Michal the daughter of Saul looked out the window and despised David in her heart as he danced and played. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing.

verses.text: And David danced before the Lord with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
And as the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.

Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

And David said unto Michal, It was before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord.
And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.
Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.

And it came to pass, as the ark of the covenant of the Lord came to the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looking out at a window saw king David dancing and playing: and she despised him in her heart.
Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.
